workshop.domainDetected: Recognised as {{domain}}. If that is wrong, pick the right kind here.
workshop.derivedBanner: Template derived. Check it under “My Templates” with the preview before activating it.

domainHints.cruise: Mark the header details (ship, booking reference, price …) and ONE row of the itinerary: its date and its port. The template reads the whole port list from that row.
domainHints.place: Mark at least the place’s name, and address, category and visit date if you like. Places read this way land in the import preview under Settings → Import.
domainHints.package: Mark the booking reference and issue date, optionally trip name, dates and price — plus ONE flight row (flight number, date, departure and arrival) and/or ONE hotel row (hotel, check-in and check-out). Each marked row becomes the rule for every row like it.
domainHints.rail: Mark the booking reference, class and price if you like — plus ONE leg: departure station, departure time, arrival station, and optionally arrival time and train. Mark the travel day where it is printed: on the row or in the heading above it.
domainHints.rental: Mark the rental company, the reservation number and, for pickup and return, the station and the date — and the time where it is printed. Without a time the end stays a day; no time is invented.

cannot.lodgingNeedsNameAndDates: Too little marked: without a property name, a check-in and a check-out this is not a stay, and a template missing those three would propose things nobody can check.
cannot.lodgingDateNotUnderstood: The date format in this mail is not read yet (month names are, purely numeric like 10.03.2026 is not). A template built on it would decline every mail this sender writes.
cannot.noDistinguishingMarker: Nothing in this mail names the sender — only this one booking. A template with no sender marker would match every stay confirmation you ever parse.
cannot.notDerivable: The workshop derives no template for this kind of document.
cannot.cruiseNeedsStopRow: A cruise needs one marked row of its itinerary: in ONE row, mark the date as “Date (itinerary)” and the port as “Port (itinerary)”. Without ports the template reads no voyage.
cannot.cruiseStopRowTooFarApart: The date and port of an itinerary day must be on the same line or on two consecutive lines (blank lines between are fine). Mark both in one entry of the port list.
cannot.cruiseStopRowNotUnderstood: No port list can be read from the marked itinerary row — there is no heading above the list, or the mark does not cover the whole port name.
cannot.dateNotUnderstood: A marked date is not read. A date like 02.06.2027 or 2 June 2027 is expected — in the itinerary also without a year, e.g. 02.06.
cannot.placeNeedsName: A place needs its name: mark what the place is called. A place without a name is not a row the import can offer.
cannot.templateReadsNothing: The derived template reads nothing from this very document, so none was saved. Check the marks.
cannot.packageNeedsBookingFields: Tour documents need a booking reference and an issue date: mark both — without them the document is no readable booking.
cannot.packageNeedsRow: Mark at least one flight row or one hotel row — a trip without a flight and without a hotel yields no proposal.
cannot.packageFlightRowIncomplete: The flight row is incomplete: mark flight number, flight date, departure (code or city) and arrival (code or city).
cannot.packageStayRowIncomplete: The hotel row is incomplete: mark hotel, check-in and check-out.
cannot.packageRowTooFarApart: The values of a row must be on the same line or on two consecutive lines (blank lines between are fine).
cannot.packageRowNotUnderstood: No rule can be built from the marked row that reads its own values back. Mark the values precisely.
cannot.railNeedsLegRow: A rail journey needs one marked leg: mark the departure station, departure time and arrival station on ONE row (arrival time and train if you like). The template reads every leg from that row.
cannot.railNeedsDate: The travel day is missing: mark the date — on the leg's row or in the heading above it (e.g. “Outbound on 14.11.2027”). Without a day every departure time would be a guess.
cannot.railRowTooFarApart: The values of one leg must sit on the same line or on two consecutive lines (blank lines in between are fine).
cannot.railRowNotUnderstood: No rule can be built from the marked leg that reads its own values back. Mark the station names and times exactly.
cannot.rentalNeedsProvider: The rental company is missing: mark its name. It is named as the issuer of every proposal this template makes.
cannot.rentalNeedsBookingFields: A rental needs more: mark the reservation number, pickup station, pickup date, return station and return date (the times if you like).
cannot.rentalEndsAmbiguous: Pickup and return carry the same label in this mail (e.g. “Station:” twice), so the template would read the same value for both ends. The workshop cannot learn such layouts yet.

preview.noSecondSample: No second sample of this kind yet. Annotate another mail from the same sender to see whether the template reads that one too.
preview.readNothing: The template would read nothing here.
preview.canActivate: The template reads its own sample — it can be activated.
preview.cannotActivate: The template does not even read its own sample. Activating it would achieve nothing.
preview.requiredFirst: Run the preview first — a template is not activated before it has read something once.
